configs.description: The chassis as it ships: two supplies in, every cage empty. The guide's package contents say the unit "includes 2 PSUs".
configs.name: base

gaps.wanted: WHAT IS PRINTED UNDER EVERY PORT COLUMN. Both instruments show a row of small light marks about 1.5 mm across below the RJ-45 block, one per column, and NEITHER RESOLVES THEM - the guide's line art at 5.03 px/mm and the datasheet photograph at 9.07 px/mm both reduce them to blur at nine times magnification. They are either a second port numbering or a second lamp row, and the face is modelled without them rather than with a guess. One enlargement of the lower edge closes this.

HOW DEEP THE THREE FAN GUARDS ARE. `edgecore/eps-fan-fixed@1` carries a 10 mm vent depth and it is an estimate: the fans are fixed, no FRU figure exists for them, and neither document dimensions the rear. The guards' FACE geometry is measured - 25.5 x 15.9 on a 47.8 pitch, agreeing between the two models' elevations to 0.2 mm - so only the depth is open.

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 2 bays (rear 2); `physical-context` on port groups rj45-1g, rj45-poe-hi, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

gate-1.note: SIX INSTRUMENTS, AND ALL SIX SAY THE HEIGHT IS 44.45 mm RATHER THAN THE SPECIFICATION TABLE'S 44. The guide's four elevations read 2215x224, 2213x224, 2213x224 and 2219x224 px; the two datasheet front photographs 3991x404 and 3998x408. Against 440 x 44 they come out -1.116%, -1.205%, -1.205%, -0.938%, -1.213% and -2.010%. Against 440 x 44.45 - true 1RU - they come out -0.105%, -0.195%, -0.195%, +0.076%, -0.203% and -1.008%. Six failures become six passes and the spread collapses by an order of magnitude, so the table's "44" is a rounding and the drawings are to 44.45. EVERY y MEASUREMENT IN THIS FILE USES THE 44.45 SCALE. On a 44 mm face the difference is half a millimetre at the bottom edge, which is the size of the features being measured. `chassis.height` still records the vendor's published 44: this is a drawing-scale fact, not a dimension change. WHICH INSTRUMENT FOR WHICH JOB, and this one is the opposite of the DCS520's. The guide's LINE ART is the geometry instrument even at 5.03 px/mm, and the datasheet PHOTOGRAPHS at 9.07 px/mm are for detail and colour - because the ganged-pitch fit below comes out with an rms of 0.082 mm on the line art and 0.74 mm on the photograph. White RJ-45 bezels are soft at 9 px/mm; a drawn edge is not.

power.note: THE POE MACHINE. "AS4625-54P: Low-line (90-136 VAC): 2000 Watts max. High-line (180-264 VAC): 2400 Watts max." power consumption at 25 C; a per-PSU system input rating of "100-120 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 12 A max. / 200-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 8.5 A max."; and a PoE budget of "Low-line: 850 W for 1 PSU, 1850 W for 2 PSUs. High-line: 1050 W for 1 PSU, 1920 W for 2 PSUs". THE PER-SUPPLY OUTPUT IS NOWHERE STATED and is not invented - the supplies' own contract omits `power-output-w` rather than guess it. THE POE SPLIT IS PRINTED ON THE PANEL. The guide's right-hand enlargement shows the legend "PoE Output: 57V ... Max., 0.53A Max/Port1-40, 1.85A Max/Port41-48", and the Overview callouts match it: "40 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (30 W per port)" and "8 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (90 W per port)". So ports 41-48 are the 90 W ones, and the panel marks them with an orange band.

sources.note: ONE QUICK START GUIDE COVERS BOTH MODELS and it is staged twice, byte-identical - md5 c81e696fe001edaa86961a6660f8da00, 1343641 bytes. Its title page reads "Ethernet Switch AS4625-54T | AS4625-54P" and its package contents "AS4625-54T/AS4625-54P (includes 2 PSUs)". Each model additionally has its own four-page datasheet with its own photographs of both faces. THE GUIDE DISCLAIMS ITS OWN DRAWINGS - "Note: The drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular model" - and on this family that is not boilerplate to ignore: see the status-lamp note below.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 3 SFP pairs (port-49/port-50 to port-53/port-54).

the-management-cluster.note: AT THE RIGHT, STACKED: an RJ-45 management jack over an RJ-45 console jack - the panel legends them "(up) Mgmt" and "Console" - with a MICRO-USB storage port below under a "USB" label. Both jacks read rows 18.75 and 30.86, which is the RJ-45 block's own row pitch to 0.12 mm, so they sit in the same stack the traffic ports do. THE MICRO-USB IS WORTH NAMING because the third member of this shell family does not have one: the EPS112's guide lists a full-size "USB storage port" where this one lists a "Micro-USB storage port". The clusters are not interchangeable between the three.

the-port-wall.note: FORTY-EIGHT RJ-45 IN TWO ROWS OF TWENTY-FOUR COLUMNS, ganged in THREE BLOCKS OF EIGHT. Fitted by least squares over all twenty-four columns with a per-block offset, on the mean of both rows' openings: **pitch 14.0158, gutter 6.4058, first centre 15.425, rms 0.082 mm, max residual 0.17**. Rows read y 14.96-22.78 and 27.29-34.66 on the photograph, centres 18.87 and 30.97, so a row pitch of 12.10. THEN SIX SFP+ AS THREE STACKED PAIRS at x 370.20, 387.98 and 405.75 - a pitch of 17.78 - with rows at 16.67 and 32.25. The SFP rows are further apart than the RJ-45 rows because that block has a divider band between its cages where the RJ-45 block has none; both were measured, neither was assumed from the other. NUMBERING IS ONE SEQUENCE ACROSS BOTH FAMILIES: RJ-45 1-48, SFP+ 49-54, legended `N (up)(down) N+1` above each column.

the-status-lamps-and-what-the-shared-gui.note: SIX LAMPS IN TWO ROWS OF THREE, on a black plate beside the Edge-core logo and the model text, with a Reset button between them. Measured on the guide's Status LEDs enlargement, calibrated on the port columns it draws (`1 (up)(down) 2` through `11 (up)(down) 12`, whose centres this file already knows exactly) at 22.62 px/mm - four and a half times the elevation: lamp columns at x 53.2, 61.0 and 68.9, rows at y 4.50 and 7.90, which the elevation's own label baselines independently confirm at 4.46 and 7.98. THE LEGEND, transcribed from the guide: System green = OK, amber = fault detected; PSU1/2 green = OK, amber = fault; FAN green = OK, amber = fault; LOC blinking amber = switch locator; PoE green = OK, amber = near PoE budget. THE ENLARGEMENT IS OF THIS MODEL - it is captioned AS4625-54P - so the six lamps and their legends are read rather than inherited. Its sibling the EPS121 is the one with the doubt: it has no PoE, and no enlargement of its own.

why-this-is-its-own-device.note: ONE GUIDE COVERS THE 54T AND THE 54P, SO THE QUESTION HAD TO BE ASKED. `docs/what-a-configuration-cannot-say.md` answers it in one sentence - a configuration can say what OCCUPIES a bay, but not what is TRUE of a part - and records that a config-scoped DEVICE attr is still open, filed as `config-scoped-device-attrs` on cisco/asr-9001. These two differ in exactly that forbidden way: weight 5.8 kg against 6.6, power consumption 150 W against 2400, per-PSU input 4 A against 12 A. The supplies really are different parts - 50.4 mm wide against 62.3, and the PoE one carries a fan - which a configuration could have expressed through `bays`; the weight and the consumption are device attrs, which it could not. And the 54P's RJ-45 row is TWO port groups where the 54T's is one, which changes the shape of the face rather than what fills it. See roc-ops/Portrayal#335 for the full working.
